title: ～あとで — “after ～ / later”
summary: あとで means ‘after ～’ when it follows a past-tense verb or noun + の, and ‘later’ when it stands alone. It states that one action happens after another. Verb た-form + あとで, noun + の + あとで.

patterns.gloss: noun + の + あとで (食事の後で)

body.p: After a verb use the plain past form: 宿題をした後で. After a noun use の: 食事の後で. The main verb can be any tense, since the tense follows the main clause.
あとで by itself means ‘later’: 後で電話します (I'll call later). It does not need a clause before it.

Both mean ‘after’. てから stresses that the second action starts only once the first is done, while ～たあとで is more neutral about order and does not stress the immediacy. Also, あとで does not require the same subject.

examples.ja: 食事（しょくじ）の後（あと）で、薬（くすり）を飲（の）みます。
examples.romaji: Shokuji no ato de, kusuri o nomimasu.

examples.ja: 宿題（しゅくだい）をした後（あと）で、遊（あそ）びに行（い）った。
examples.romaji: Shukudai o shita ato de, asobi ni itta.
examples.tr: After I did my homework, I went out to play.
examples.note: した is the plain past of する.

examples.ja: 今（いま）は忙（いそが）しいので、後（あと）で電話（でんわ）します。
examples.romaji: Ima wa isogashii node, ato de denwa shimasu.
examples.tr: I'm busy right now, so I'll call you later.

pitfalls: Use the ta-form before 後で: 食べた後で, not 食べる後で.
After a noun you need の: 食事の後で, not 食事後で (the latter is written style, 食事後).
